name: Legendary Warpriest
body:
The warpriest is the right hand of their deity, a sword wielded against their foes. Their entire purpose is to fight the enemies of their deity and exemplify their tenants on the battlefield.

Their faith and the portfolio of their deity informs how they conquer the battlefield, for the warpriest of the god of nature would differ much from the warpriest of the god of deceit.

Why do the legendary warpriests? What will change? The original warpriest had very little variation from warpriest to warpriest as the only major build difference is the two blessings which only grant differing powers at 1st and 10th levels, the remainder of the abilities are shared and are focused on one kind of warpriest. The legendary warpriest will take a cue from the Legendary Cleric and have more of its abilities vary based upon their deity’s blessings. So, the major change will be, less static abilities and more abilities focused upon the blessing provided by their faith.

Role: The legendary warpriest is a frontline support and secondary combatant.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Requirements

Alignment: A legendary warpriest’s alignment must be within one step of their deity’s, along either the law/chaos axis or the good/evil axis.

Class Skills

The legendary warpriest’s class skills are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are the class features of the legendary warpriest.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A legendary warpriest is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, as well as the favored weapon of their deity, and with all armor (heavy, light, and medium) and shields (except tower shields). If the warpriest worships a deity with unarmed strike as its favored weapon, the warpriest gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat.

Spellcasting

A legendary warpriest casts divine spells drawn from the legendary warpriest spell list, see below.

Their alignment, however, can restrict them from casting certain spells opposed to their moral or ethical beliefs; see the Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells section. A legendary warpriest must choose and prepare their spells in advance.

To prepare or cast a spell, a legendary warpriest must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell’s level. The saving throw DC against a legendary warpriest’s spell is 10 + the spell’s level + the legendary warpriest’s Wisdom modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a legendary warpriest can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table 1-2 Spells per Day. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Wisdom score.

Legendary warpriests meditate or pray for their spells.

Each legendary warpriest must choose a time when they must spend 1 hour each day in quiet contemplation or supplication to regain their daily allotment of spells. A legendary warpriest can prepare and cast any spell on their spell list, provided that they can cast spells of that level, but they must choose which spells to prepare during their daily meditation.

Orisons: Legendary warpriests can prepare a number of orisons, or 0-level spells, each day as noted on Table 1-2 Spells per Day. These spells are cast as any other spell, but aren’t expended when cast and can be used again.

Spontaneous Casting: A legendary warpriest can channel stored spell energy into spells listed in the domains provided by their deity or faith that they did not prepare ahead of time.

When praying for their spells for the day, the warpriest may choose one spell of each level, available to them from their domains, to be their spontaneous spells for the day. The legendary warpriest can expend any prepared spell that isn’t an orison to cast any spell from that list of the same spell level or lower.

Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells: A legendary warpriest cannot cast spells of an alignment opposed to their own or their deity’s (if they have a deity). Spells associated with particular alignments are indicated by the chaotic, evil, good, and lawful descriptors in their spell descriptions.

Legendary Warpriest Spell List: The legendary warpriest gains a select number of spells They can pray for from their deity or faith. They add all the spells from the list laid out in the Legendary Warpriest Spell List section on page xx to their spell list. In addition, at 1st level and every level thereafter they may add two spells to their spell list from the sections of choices laid out in the domains available to their deity or faith.

The spells added to their spell list must be of a spell level they can cast. The spell being available as a domain spell does not allow the warpriest to prepare the spell in a spell slot.

For example, a 1st-level legendary warpriest of the god of magic gains all the 0-level and 1st-level spells from the legendary warpriest spell list. Then because they have access to the knowledge and magic domains via their deity, for the two spells they add to their spell list at 1st level, they can pick any wizard spell or divination spell of 1st level or lower.

If the spell appears at different levels on different spell lists, follow the level hierarchy used by spell-like abilities and treat any spell only on a 4th-level spell list (such as the paladin or ranger list) as one level higher.

Aura (Ex)

A legendary warpriest of a chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity has a particularly powerful aura (as a cleric) corresponding to the deity’s alignment (see detect evil).

Blessing

A legendary warpriest is invested by their deity or faith to carry out combat in their name. Having been given such a charter, they are granted blessings that empower them in battle. At 1st level and every odd level thereafter, the legendary warpriest may gain a blessing provided by one of the domains accessible by their deity or faith. Unless otherwise stated a blessing can only be chosen once and the legendary warpriest must meet its prerequisites.

Instead of a blessing, the legendary warpriest may select a combat feat or the Extra Fervor feat. They must meet the prerequisites of the feat chosen. For the purposes of these feats, the warpriest can select feats that have a minimum number of fighter levels as a prerequisite, treating their warpriest level as their fighter level.

Weapons of the Faithful (Ex)

A legendary warpriest gains a +1 attack bonus to all weapons in a weapon group determined by their deity or faith. The weapon group is any weapon belonging to a weapon group from which the deity’s or faith’s favored weapon comes from. If the weapon is from multiple weapon groups, the legendary warpriest chooses one and the decision cannot be changed later. For example, if the legendary warpriest’s deity has their favored weapon as the dagger, the war priest could choose the light blades or thrown weapon group. The warpriest is considered proficient with all weapons in the chosen group if they are not already.

This bonus increases by +1 at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.)

Bonus Languages

A legendary warpriest’s bonus language options include Abyssal, Celestial, and Infernal. These choices are in addition to the bonus languages available to the character because of their race.

Fervor: Beginning at 2nd level, a legendary warpriest can cast a spell they have prepared with a casting time of 1 round or shorter as a swift action. When cast in this way, 6 the spell can only target the warpriest, even if it could normally target other or multiple targets. Spells cast in this way ignore somatic components and do not provoke attacks of opportunity. The warpriest does not need to have a free hand to cast a spell in this way. The warpriest may use this ability a number of times per day equal to 1/2 their legendary warpriest level + their Wisdom modifier.

Instead of quickening their spellcasting, the legendary warpriest can channel divine energy. Starting at 2nd level, as a standard action that expends a use of fervor, they can heal or harm themselves or a target (by channeling positive or negative energy) with a touch. If they use this ability on themselves, it is a swift action. At 2nd level they heal or inflict 1d6 plus their Wisdom modifier in damage. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, this healing or harming goes up by 1d6.

Instead of healing or harming at a touch, they can expend two uses of fervor to have the healing or harming affect all creatures within 30 feet as if by a cleric’s channel energy. This use of fervor is treated as channel energy for prerequisites, feats and other abilities, though it does not stack with the uses of channel energy provided by other classes. However, Extra Channel does not allow for additional uses of this ability, only Extra Fervor can.

Sacred Defense (Su)

Beginning at 4th level, a legendary warpriest is granted a boon of protection from their deity or faith. They gain a sacred defense at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter. The sacred defense abilities can be chosen multiple times, granting additional bonuses or uses. The legendary warpriest’s sacred defense is active so long as they maintain at least 1 use of fervor. The legendary warpriest gains the benefits of all of the sacred defense options they have chosen at once and the benefits of each stack if they overlap.

Avatar of War (Su)

At 20th level, the legendary warpriest is a scion of combat in the name of their faith. They may choose one of the avatar abilities from amongst the domains available to their deity or faith. When their sacred defense is active they can expend a use of fervor as a standard action to gain these additional avatar of war benefits for 1 minute.

If this would expend the warpriest’s final use of fervor, the legendary warpriest still gains the benefits of their sacred defense while the duration of this ability is active.

Legendary Warpriest Spell List

0-Level Spells–bleed, detect magic, guidance, light, read magic, stabilize, virtue

1st-Level Spells–bane, bless, bless water, cure light wounds, curse water, divine favor, inflict light wounds, shield of faith

2nd-Level Spells–aid, augury, bear’s endurance, bull’s strength, consecrate, cure moderate wounds, desecrate, eagle’s splendor, inflict moderate wounds, owl’s wisdom, resist energy, spiritual weapon

3rd-Level Spells–channel vigor, cure serious wounds, dispel magic, inflict serious wounds, prayer, protection from energy, sacred bond

4th-Level Spells–blessing of fervor, cure critical wounds, divination, divine power, inflict critical wounds, spiritual ally

5th-Level Spells–commune, hallow, mass cure light wounds, mass inflict light wounds

6th-Level Spells–greater dispel magic, harm, heal, mass bear’s endurance, mass bull’s strength, mass cure moderate wounds, mass eagle’s splendor, mass inflict moderate wounds, mass owl’s wisdom
